id_and_class.theory_title: Merleau-Ponty's Embodied Perception and the Lived Body
id_and_class.summary: Maurice Merleau-Ponty locates consciousness in the lived body and its pre-reflective, motor engagement with a world that shows up as a field of solicitations, obstacles, and possibilities. He argues that the atomic ‘sensation’ most theories start from is an artifact of analysis, and he recasts consciousness from ‘I think’ to ‘I can’, a bodily power of grip and orientation. His late ontology of ‘flesh’ treats perceiver and perceived as reversible aspects of one fabric of being.
id_and_class.core_identity_tagline: Consciousness as the Lived Body’s Engagement With a World

conceptual_ground.explanatory_identity_claim: Consciousness is the lived body's pre-reflective openness to a meaningful world, perceptual, motor, affective, spatial, temporal, and intersubjective, and inseparable from the world it discloses.
conceptual_ground.ontological_status: Ontology of flesh (neither materialism nor dualism)
conceptual_ground.mind_body_relationship: The body-subject is neither an object nor an instrument of a separate mind; it is the subject's concrete way of existing. In the late work, the mind–body problem is dissolved by rejecting the objectivist ontology that produced both terms, not by reducing one to the other.
conceptual_ground.emergence_type: Not applicable. Merleau-Ponty rejects the split between inner experience and outer matter that the question of emergence assumes, treating sentient and sensible as aspects of one flesh.
conceptual_ground.subjectivity_and_intentionality: Intentionality is bodily before it is mental. Motor intentionality, the hand drawn toward a cup without computing a trajectory, works in union with the explicit intentionality of judgment and thought.
conceptual_ground.qualia_account: There are no inner qualia inspected by a subject. Sensory presence belongs to the perceptual field as the body discloses it, and the explanatory gap is a symptom of ‘objective thought’, not a deep fact about nature.
conceptual_ground.ontological_commitments: The lived body (le corps propre) as distinct from the anatomical body; the body schema; a pre-objective phenomenal field organized as Gestalt wholes; in late work, flesh (la chair) as an element of being.
conceptual_ground.epistemic_access: Phenomenological description combined with neurology, Gestalt psychology, and pathology, using breakdowns (brain injury, phantom limb) to expose structures that normal functioning hides.
conceptual_ground.constituents_and_structure: The body schema (schéma corporel), a dynamic, pre-reflective organization of posture and capacity; a perceptual field of ambiguity and context; in late work, the chiasm, in which seer and seen intertwine.

mechanism_and_dynamics.scope_of_consciousness: Phenomenal (perceptual); agency and motor skill; embodiment; spatiality; intersubjectivity.
mechanism_and_dynamics.distinctive_mechanism_or_principle: Motor intentionality and maximal grip: skilled bodies move toward optimal purchase on their situation without representing a goal.
mechanism_and_dynamics.dynamics_of_emergence: Perception is an ongoing bodily engagement in which the world and the body's powers shape each other.
mechanism_and_dynamics.location_and_distribution: In the lived body engaged with its surroundings, not in an inner theater or in the brain alone.
mechanism_and_dynamics.causation_and_functional_role: Consciousness discloses a world organized by bodily capacities: a doorway shows up as walk-through-able, a glass as reachable.
mechanism_and_dynamics.integration_or_binding: The body schema unifies posture and capacity, and perceptual fields are organized wholes from the start, so no synthesis from atomic sensations is required.
mechanism_and_dynamics.information_flow_or_representation: The world shows up first as solicitations, not neutral information. Hubert Dreyfus reads Merleau-Ponty as showing that skilled action needs no mental representation.
core_claims_and_evidence: Empiricism and intellectualism both presuppose the structured perceptual field they claim to build from sensations or judgments.

Schneider, a brain-injured patient described by Kurt Goldstein, could make concrete situated movements but failed at abstract movements on command, which isolates motor intentionality as its own layer.
Phantom limb is explained by a body still committed to a world it can no longer inhabit, which neither physiology nor psychology alone accounts for.
The touching-touched hand shows that sentient and sensible are reversible aspects of one flesh.
mechanism_and_dynamics.basis_of_belief_or_evidence_type: Phenomenological, drawing on clinical neurology, Gestalt psychology, and pathology.

empirics_and_critiques.known_empirical_interventions_or_tests: Clinical cases such as Goldstein's patient Schneider and phantom limb; his ideas seeded sensorimotor theory (O'Regan and Noë, 2001), enactivism, and Gallagher's body schema / body image distinction.
empirics_and_critiques.criticisms_and_tensions: Critics such as Taylor Carman and Timothy Mooney caution that cognitive science flattens Merleau-Ponty, whose aims were ontological, not a theory of perception. His proficient, athletic body has been charged with idealizing away age and disability. In the late ontology, reversibility implies continuity while divergence (écart) implies separation, and Merleau-Ponty did not settle the tension.
empirics_and_critiques.open_questions_and_limitations: Merleau-Ponty never poses the hard problem. Whether his view dissolves it or relocates it without answering it remains open, and the ontology of flesh was left unfinished.
empirics_and_critiques.ontological_coherence: He judged his own earlier framework to retain a residual dualism and replaced it with the ontology of flesh, which seeks a position that is neither reductive materialism nor dualism.

AI_consciousness.rationale: Since consciousness here is the lived body's motor engagement with a world, a disembodied computational system would lack what consciousness consists in. Merleau-Ponty did not address machines.

survival_beyond_death.rationale: It follows from the view that consciousness is the lived body's engagement with the world, so it does not outlast the body.

meaning_and_purpose.rationale: Meaning arises in bodily, perceptual, and intersubjective engagement with the world, with no appeal to a transcendent purpose.

virtual_immortality.rationale: A copy of information without a lived body engaged with a world would lack the body-subject that consciousness is.
